Here's a summary:\n\n## Root cause\n\nIn `sympy/polys/matrices/normalforms.py`, `_hermite_normal_form` only processed the bottom `min(m, n)` rows of the matrix:\n\n```python\nrows = min(m, n)\nfor i in range(m - 1, m - 1 - rows, -1):\n```\n\nFor an m×n matrix with more rows than columns (m > n), the top `m - n` rows were never examined. This caused rows to be silently dropped: the algorithm would skip a row whose candidate pivot entry was 0 (concluding it was a zero row), re-use the same pivot column for the next row up — but that next row was never processed because the loop had already stopped. The result was a rank-deficient output.\n\nFor the reported example, the 3×2 input `[[1, 12], [0, 8], [0, 5]]` (rank 2) came out as `[[12], [8], [5]]` (rank 1), because row 1 was skipped and row 0 — where the second pivot belongs — was never reached.\n\n## Fix\n\nProcess **all** rows, breaking out early once `k == 0` (when all `n` columns already have pivots — the maximum possible). This is exactly the fix adopted upstream in SymPy 1.12:\n\n- `for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1):` with a `if k == 0: break` guard before decrementing the pivot column.\n\n## Test updates\n\nTwo tests (in `sympy/polys/matrices/tests/test_normalforms.py` and `sympy/matrices/tests/test_normalforms.py`) pinned the old buggy behavior for `[[2, 7], [0, 0], [0, 0]]` (expecting a 3×0 matrix, i.e., rank 0). Here's a summary:\n\n## Root cause\n\nIn `sympy/polys/matrices/normalforms.py`, `_hermite_normal_form` only processed the bottom `min(m, n)` rows of the matrix:\n\n```python\nrows = min(m, n)\nfor i in range(m - 1, m - 1 - rows, -1):\n```\n\nFor an m×n matrix with more rows than columns (m > n), the top `m - n` rows were never examined. This caused rows to be silently dropped: the algorithm would skip a row whose candidate pivot entry was 0 (concluding it was a zero row), re-use the same pivot column for the next row up — but that next row was never processed because the loop had already stopped. The result was a rank-deficient output.\n\nFor the reported example, the 3×2 input `[[1, 12], [0, 8], [0, 5]]` (rank 2) came out as `[[12], [8], [5]]` (rank 1), because row 1 was skipped and row 0 — where the second pivot belongs — was never reached.\n\n## Fix\n\nProcess **all** rows, breaking out early once `k == 0` (when all `n` columns already have pivots — the maximum possible).
